summary: The study reports the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of copper thin films with (111) texture on oxidized Si(100) surfaces using Cu(thd)2 as a precursor. The films exhibit strong (111) texture, large grain size, and high conductivity. The process was carried out at a deposition temperature of 3501C, and the films showed low resistivity and high resistance to electromigration. The ALD process was found to produce highly conformal and textured copper films suitable for VLSI metallization.
evidence: Copper ﬁlms with (111) texture are of crucial importance in integrated circuit interconnects. We have deposited strongly (111)-textured thin ﬁlms of copper by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using [2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-3,5-heptadionato]Cu(II), Cu(thd)2, as the precursor. The (111) texture of the ALD-grown copper ﬁlms was studied further by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The films exhibit strong (111) texture, large grain size, and high conductivity. The film thickness varies linearly with the number of ALD cycles, and the average thickness of copper deposited per cycle is about two monolayers. The resistivity of the film grown at 3501C for 720 ALD cycles is 1.7mOcm, effectively the bulk value.
